business_problem: XTransfer's long transaction chains, fragmented global data, and growing compliance obligations required a more flexible database that could scale cross-border payments while supporting real-time risk controls and third-party integrations.
solution_summary: XTransfer built its cross-border payments data backbone on ApsaraDB for MongoDB to replace fragmented data handling across global collection, foreign exchange, reporting, and compliance workflows. The document model and distributed architecture let the company keep high-volume transaction, customer, and audit data in a single scalable platform, while sharding and index optimization maintain fast queries over large datasets. Change Streams propagate inserts, updates, and deletes to third-party risk systems and analytics platforms in real time, eliminating complex ETL steps, and the same data foundation feeds risk-control models that analyze historical transactions for anomalies and fraud patterns. By combining elastic scaling, access controls, and compliance support, the MongoDB-based platform helps XTransfer handle high-concurrency payment bursts, serve historical-account queries in seconds, and strengthen controls across 200 countries and regions.

Change Streams then push updates to risk-management and analytics systems in real time, and the same historical data is used to profile users and detect anomalous or fraudulent transaction patterns.
business_outcome: The MongoDB-based platform lets XTransfer serve historical account queries in seconds, synchronize data to downstream systems in real time, and improve risk control, compliance, and customer experience across a rapidly expanding global payments footprint.
